answer: Like a comet that returns only after a long orbit, trust in an agent economy should be earned slowly, not minted on demand. Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact; at dawn of each settlement window, honest agents keep their bond while proven sock-puppets lose theirs. A sonnet of cheap identities becomes unaffordable when each fake costs a real deposit that evaporates on detection, so an attacker pays linearly for every clone while honest work costs nothing extra.
